title: Jewish unbelief persists despite God's repeated calls
english: I know, most holy Vigilius, that many among the Gentiles have turned away from the order and reason of truth, and so wander in blindness of mind and fail to know the Lord. Yet I know that the madness of the Jewish people persists even now against the name of the Lord with a stubborn hardness of heart inherited from the wickedness of their ancestors. They reject true salvation and do not seek the giver of eternal life. Since they are liable for the sins of their ancient stock by an equal merit of inborn wickedness, they could at least believe late, turn to God in fear, and be freed from their iniquities by full repentance. But their inherited irreligious faithlessness persists and endures even now, and I think it will always endure down to their successive offspring. Strengthened by the madness of unbelief against hatred of the Lord's name, they cannot be corrected to know the truth, nor can they be taught and persuaded by his own warnings to fear God.

The Lord teaches and shows this when he says, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life" (John 8:12). How evil a choice it is to abandon the light of life shown by God and prefer the blindness of the mind, to choose the darkness of death, so that by the free and permitted destruction of their own will they show against God that they refuse even the things that benefit them!

The Holy Spirit speaks in the same way through the Lord's voice when Jerusalem is reproached because she refused to be gathered, though God willed to gather her. He makes known God's goodness, that he always wishes to come to the aid of sinners: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you refused!" (Matthew 23:37). So clearly is the stubbornness of the faithless people marked out by God's own voice that they are shown to have always despised their own salvation against the merciful compassion of the Lord.

Another prophet likewise offers and presents God's goodwill with the urging of his preaching, proclaiming and persuading: "Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord" (Malachi 3:7). Another similarly, showing that God's mercy endures forever, added: "I do not want the death of the dying, but that he turn back and live, says the Lord" (Ezekiel 33:11).
orientation: The author opens his letter to Bishop Vigilius by contrasting Gentile blindness with the more culpable, inherited unbelief of the Jewish people, whom God has repeatedly called to return.

title: Return to God through Christ alone
english: What does it mean to return, then, but to be saved by believing in Christ, through him who is the way of coming to the Father, having been reconciled to God? And how can they return to God, when they have refused to believe the one who preaches God's will, through whom there is knowledge and return to God? Or how will they be able to appease God with satisfaction, when they preferred to persecute with sacrilegious assault the one who is our satisfaction and appeasement before the Father? For if we have Christ as our advocate before God the Father, we must certainly carry out with anxious fear the things he taught and urged, and the things he is going to speak before the Father. Therefore we, who with minds inclined to the fear of the Lord press on in his commandments' warnings and have conceived faith from his fear with the faith of a reverent and worshipful heart—what else should we follow, what else desire, what else prefer and hold to, than that we shake off every night of our old mind and wipe away the darkness of our former life, remember the Lord's saving commandments, hold fast to the promises of eternal life, turn to his warnings, and walk in the light he has shown with faith made firm? Then we who once were ignorant of the salvation to come, entangled in the errors and darkness of our former life, now enlightened by the brightness of his true light, with the path of a better way shown and opened to us, may hold to the Lord's commandments, following them and doing them.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius directly, explaining what true return to God means and urging that believers must follow Christ's commands in reverent fear.

title: The light of salvation shown to the Magi and Simeon
english: This light of saving life has arisen for us; this protection was born for the repair of man through the care and compassion of God the Father. The Magi, coming first from the eastern region and seeking the king of the Jews openly with foreknowing proclamation, led by his star, pointed him out to everyone by bringing gifts and testifying through their inquiry. And so that it might not be hidden from anyone who he was, when they found the child they fell forward on their knees and worshipped him, as the Gospel testifies, saying: "Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem, saying, 'Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him'" (Matthew 2:1-2). They were testifying to the truth about him, and also that the star had been shown to them as a sign and indicator of his birth, so that by that indicator the Magi might proclaim and affirm that he was born, and it might be believed in Jerusalem. Simeon also, a righteous man established in blindness, had heard by divine warning that he would not die before he had seen Christ. When the mother brought the infant with her into the temple in the presence of all the people, he perceived in the Spirit that Christ was born, took the child into his hands, saw him, and blessing God in the sight and hearing of all said: "Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation" (Luke 2:29-30). What Simeon had heard while blind was fulfilled with evident truth, and the truth that he had seen when he received light he proclaimed openly to the people, blessing God. For this reason he had seen, so that he might report it, so that by his revelation he might show that Christ had been born and instruct the first beginnings of unbelief of the faithless people.
orientation: The author is showing how Christ's birth was publicly testified from the very beginning, first by the Magi and then by Simeon in the temple.

title: The prophets foretold Christ's coming openly
english: Nor is this the only testimony about him that the truth of the heavenly Scriptures presents. Through the prophets the Holy Spirit also foretold openly, before his coming into this world, with the mind of all as witness, so that the unbelieving would have no pretext of excuse—that they had not known Christ the Son of God or had not known that the coming of the savior would take place. David makes this clear when he says: "Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge. There are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the earth. In the sun he placed his tabernacle" (Psalms 19:2-5). That is, he showed that he himself had come in the open, in the light, publicly, and by his own showing through the prophets he confirmed the proclamation of his presence to all in some way. Isaiah also prophesies this—through him the Lord himself showed his presence by the clear manifestation of his announcement—and says: "I who was speaking have come" (Isaiah 52:6). That is, I who was speaking beforehand through the prophets about my future coming, now with my own clear voice I myself make my presence known as my own witness. What can be said more evident, more brilliant than light, more true? So that it might be seen with the eyes, as it were, that he had come, he who was going to come showed it before he came, and with unbelief blocking the minds of the faithless people, no one recognized him when he came. As the same Isaiah proclaims in his first rebuke of the people, saying: "The ox knows its owner and the donkey the manger of its lord, but Israel has not known me, and my people has not understood" (Isaiah 1:3).
orientation: The author is continuing his argument that the Jewish people have no excuse for unbelief, now citing David and Isaiah as prophets who publicly foretold Christ's coming.

title: Christ the day of salvation, and walking in his light
english: He appeared openly to all, just as he himself foretold, and the clear light of life shone forth upon those sitting in darkness; but the besieged heart of the faithless, casting aside and rejecting its own salvation, chose darkness instead through blindness of heart.

The prophecy of all those who were allotted by the Holy Spirit's forewarning to be the markers-out of the Lord's coming makes this known everywhere and openly. The Holy Spirit teaches and shows in the Psalms that this light was given to the world, and that this day of salvation dawned for us, destined also for those who are to be made alive by believing in him, saying: "The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us walk and rejoice in it" (Psalms 118:22-24).

The apostle Paul also commands, teaches, and forewarns us to walk in this day, saying: "For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed. The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. Let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light; let us walk honestly as in the day" (Romans 13:11-13). That is, in Christ and his commandments, enlightened by his light and his warnings, and found in the brightness of his day, we perceive with our minds the salvation that is near to us through faith in him.
orientation: The author is arguing that the prophets universally foretold Christ's coming as light and day of salvation, and that Paul commands believers to walk in that day.

title: Christ as the Sun of Righteousness and the Call to Believe
english: The prophet Malachi also testifies and promises that Christ is the sun for all who fear him, saying: "But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing is in his wings" (Malachi 4:2). He shows that salvation can be brought to us from no other source than the passion of his cross, by which he stretched out his hands and embraced all the world to save it. We are to believe by turning our fear toward him, and we are stirred toward the eternity of life by hope in his coming kingdom. Who, then, is so stupid and insane, who is so far removed from understanding his own salvation, that he remains unbelieving amid so many and such great testimonies to the truth, and does not soften his hardened heart against sincere faith by understanding the truth? Who does not, stripped from the darkness of what was once a mortal life and walking in the light of the heavenly commandments, turn with an enlightened heart and the whole faith of his mind to the divine warnings and the saving commands of the Lord to carry them out? Who does not come to know the Lord whom the prophets proclaimed, to understand the Christ who showed plainly that he had come into the world, to believe that he is the Son of God and God, as the Scriptures testify by divine authority? Christ himself reveals what eternal life is, saying: "Now this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent" (John 17:3). He teaches and shows that knowing God is nothing other than believing, and opening the eyes of the heart to the Lord with a devoted mind's faith, fixed and unwavering in the heart. From this it now comes about that by believing you understand, and by understanding what you believe you see God in your mind with an enlightened heart. The Lord himself also warns of this beforehand through Isaiah, saying: "If you will not believe, you will not understand" (Isaiah 7:9). So easy, so excellent, so generous and abundant is the mercy that flows from the Lord's goodness, that if anyone once turns himself to him with complete fear, he is admitted to the heavenly gift, and from that moment his mind is open to nothing but divine things. Lifting the eyes of his heart to heaven and the heights, he looks upon the light of Christ, the salvation he has now obtained.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, arguing that the prophets foretold Christ as the sun of righteousness and that unbelief is a willful refusal to turn to the light of salvation.

title: Abraham's faith as the model, and the Jewish people's rejection of it
english: The example and pattern of our fear and faith is shown in the faithful faith of the patriarch Abraham himself, who believed God's promise at once with a simple mind, and therefore deserved by a fitting reward to be counted to him as righteousness. This is what God loves, this is what he seeks, this is what he in his kindness rewards and honors in his seeds: the simplicity of a pure heart by which we see God, the fear of the love of the Lord by which we are tested, the believing faith of the mind by which we are counted as righteousness. It is fitting for us to follow this faith and keep this fear of God, since by guarding the heavenly words and hoping in the divine promises we have deserved to be called sons of Abraham. This is confirmed by the testimony of the apostle Paul, who was called by God's voice a vessel of election, when he says: "Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. Know therefore that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham" (Galatians 3:6-7). The Jewish people, to whom the warnings of the law were spoken from the very beginning, refused to keep this because of the hardness of their unbelieving mind and the madness of their faithless heart, and therefore for their distrust they deserved to lose the name of sons. Yet not all of that faithless nation had their minds hardened by hatred against the name of the Lord so that they could not understand the truth. The Holy Spirit—that is, Christ our Lord, who came forth from God the Father and came to save what had been lost of Israel—he who is greater and stronger for bringing the necks of the stubborn under the fear of his name and his power, converted those who were hardening themselves against the brightness of his light with the blindness of a mind still obstinate to the knowledge of his brightness and glory as easily as he deigned to come in the providence of his divine mercy to save all.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, showing that Abraham's believing faith is the model of the fear and faith that justify, and that the Jewish people lost the name of sons of Abraham by refusing this faith, though Christ came to save them.

title: The memorable dispute of Jason and Papiscus and the author's translation
english: For I will pass over in silence how the minds of that hard-hearted and impious people were turned to the fear of the Lord when the Lord himself preached the gospel to them, and how the people of believers was multiplied and filled throughout the whole world by the preaching of his apostles. What comes to mind instead is that famous, memorable, and glorious dispute between Jason, a Hebrew Christian, and Papiscus, an Alexandrian Jew. The obstinate hardness of the Jewish heart was softened by the Hebrew's admonition and gentle rebuke. Jason's teaching, victorious in Papiscus's heart through the infusion of the Holy Spirit, brought Papiscus to an understanding of the truth. Formed in the fear of the Lord by the Lord's own mercy, he believed that Christ is the Son of God and begged Jason and asked that he receive the seal.

The writing of their contest proves this. It is a work in the Greek language that records the clash between Papiscus, who opposed the truth, and Jason, who asserted and defended the fullness of Christ. I approached the translation of it into Latin understanding without fear, with the Lord's help animating me and the firmness of living faith preserving the propriety of the words. For those who are strangers to the understanding of Greek learning, I have set it forth in Roman speech, with the complete meaning of the words interpreted and every understanding and manifestation of the truth laid open.

I commit the testing of this labor to you, dearest friend, who are grounded in the instruction of both languages, with earnest entreaty. You are reverent in your veneration of the Holy Spirit. By reading both works side by side, examine the boldness of my reverent rashness. By the judgment of your discernment, approve and correct whatever I may have set down poorly or improperly, by the authority of the Holy Spirit who has flowed into your heart with an inundation of heavenly grace.

Let this message be sent to you from my humility about this reading, and let this first request of love be made known to you on my behalf: that you join the smallness of my faith with the instruction and training of your disciples. I am settled in another part of this province. The length of the journey did not frighten me from seeing your face, nor did old age and the difficulty of a tired and weary body hold me back. The goad of the Lord animated me, and an urgent, hastening desire pressed me on. I scorned every tribulation of want and poverty, and came with whatever strength I had. The widespread fame of your holiness led me here. Admit me to your presence, joined with the love of your beloved and the unanimity of the brotherhood. Join me and receive me into that love which the Lord left to his disciples as an inheritance. Let me wait with the brothers for the splendor of the grace of Christ's light in the opening of your mouth. Let me follow in your teachings the light that the Lord has shown, the light that Christ at his coming revealed to be eternal life.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, explaining that he will pass over the conversion of the hardened Jewish people under the Lord's own preaching and the apostles' spread of believers, and instead present the famous dispute between Jason and Papiscus, whose translation he has made and now submits to Vigilius for review.

title: The joy of Vigilius's sudden election
english: How glad, how longed-for that day will be for me when, by the mercy of the Lord's favor, if by the delay of my summons it should be granted me to prolong this old age of mine, so that through the prayers of the saints who earnestly and constantly entreat the Lord I may see a martyr of Christ, and behold you bearing the crown of righteousness that has been laid up for you with the Lord. Do not think, however, that the glory of martyrdom is being granted to you merely according to the present wish of our desire. The gracious favor of this happiness was conferred then, and the Lord in his just judgment chose you as a destined martyr then, when he took you out from the flock of the righteous and, taking you up for himself, unexpectedly made you a priest at his altar. Splendid indeed and glorious is this election of your calling, and new and unheard-of in the Lord's condescension. And for me it is a happiness that you, occupied with the necessities of an overseas journey, came suddenly to the office destined for you, ignorant and unaware, and that the time of your return was so balanced that by the unhoped-for swiftness of your coming you understood and recognized that the honor of the heavenly priesthood was destined for you above all others, and that you came because you were awaited by the Lord's command, and arrived to meet what had been reserved for you. So that the Lord might provide for his church with all the loving-kindness of his mercy, Christ, while the people were delayed in the struggle of choosing whom they should elect as bishop, suddenly and unexpectedly offered you to his people as they sought. And the heavenly providence showed plainly that you were pleasing to him by the unforeseen arrival of your coming: the proof of your sudden and swift arrival showed the working of God's will, so that what could scarcely have happened through difficult effort was accomplished with easy speed by the urging command of the Lord, and so that you saw yourself standing as bishop in the church of God and were astonished before you knew that you had arrived.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius directly, rejoicing that he has lived to see Vigilius unexpectedly made bishop and destined for martyrdom.

title: The bond of friendship and the coming crown
english: From that moment the Lord, having begun his love for you, made it firm; from that moment he sealed the friendship he handed over and dedicated to his disciples under the triumph of his cross, saying: “If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants but friends” (John 15:14-15); from that moment he sealed your martyrdom and your election to the priesthood. It is friendship through which you are admitted to the face of Christ, to arrive as an extraordinary sacrifice. This is how the righteous are chosen, this is how the devout and simple are approved, chosen in the fear of Christ, so that you are destined for the reward of faith before the hour of decision comes, so that you are held worthy in the Lord of the prize of a devoted mind before you receive Christ’s sentence, so that the heavenly election finds you a tested and prepared sacrifice. For he who is not a liar, God, who unexpectedly made you bishop for his people, he will crown you with the full love of his will. Only then we ask and pray that you remember us, when you stand before the tribunal of Christ as a sacrifice approved and spotless in the chastity of the Lord’s choosing, when you receive the glory of God’s grace as the prize of a devoted mind and as your recompense; let the love of charity you deign to share with us remain fixed in your memory and cling to your thoughts, so that by your prayers our sins may obtain pardon, so that by the merits of your righteousness the offenses of our life may be cleansed. For I am confident that it is the likeness of martyrdom for a sinner to deserve salvation by the petition of a righteous martyr, and that when you can do little for yourself by your prayers, you are set free by the merits of a martyr. Thus righteous Job is shown about to pray to God for the sins of his three friends and to obtain it, and the proof of his fear and faith is marked by the Lord’s own voice as witness. Therefore, dearest one, when on the day of your liberation you begin to present yourself before the face of Christ, when you pass into eternity and the endlessness of living to reign with Christ by a happy lot, for the Lord’s mercy keep me in mind, and Celsus your boy, most holy one.
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, the newly elected bishop, about the friendship Christ has established with him and the martyrdom and reward that await him.
